{{Short description|In statistics, a continuous time random walk}}
{{One source|date=September 2025}}

In [[statistics]], a '''generalized Wiener process'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Stochastic Processes and Monte Carlo Method {{!}} Introduction To Options on QuantConnect |url=https://www.quantconnect.com/learning/articles/introduction-to-options/stochastic-processes-and-monte-carlo-method |website=quantconnect.com |access-date=13 September 2025 |language=en}}</ref> (named after [[Norbert Wiener]]) is a [[continuous time]] [[random walk with drift]] and [[random]] jumps at every point in time. Formally:

:<math>a(x,t) dt + b(x,t) \eta \sqrt{dt}</math>

where a and b are [[deterministic]] functions, t is a [[continuous function|continuous]] index for time, x is a set of [[exogenous]] variables that may change with time, dt is a [[differential of a function|differential]] in time, and η is a [[random]] draw from a [[standard normal distribution]] at each instant.
